rows.label: Formula
rows.text:
dθ/dt = −k (θ − θ0)
k = K /(mc)

rows.label: Conditions
rows.text: The rate of cooling is dθ/dt, not the heat itself.  ·  k is not the same for two bodies just because they are in the same room.

rows.label: Special cases
rows.text: K grows with surface area.  ·  A fan adds forced convection and takes the situation outside the simple law.

rows.label: Solved
rows.text: Newton's law of cooling says that, when the excess temperature is not large, the rate of loss of heat is proportional to the excess of the body's temperature over the surroundings.  ·  If the heat loss is dQ in time dt, then dQ/dt = K (θ − θ0), where K depends on the exposed area and the nature of the surface, and θ0 is the surrounding temperature.

rows.label: Limitation
rows.text: The law does not say the temperature falls at a constant rate.  ·  θ0 is the surroundings, not the initial temperature of the body.

rows.text: Connection of Newton's Law of Cooling — Derivation of Rate of Fall of Temperature to other topics  ·  The rate of cooling is proportional to the excess temperature.  ·  The law is for a small excess.  ·  k depends on surface and on mc.

rows.text: Two bodies have the same surface constant K and the same excess temperature. Their heat capacities are mc and 2mc. Compare the initial rates of fall of temperature.

rows.text: Newton's law, in its linear form, says the heat-loss rate is proportional to → B  ·  A smaller mc, with the same surface, makes the temperature → A

rows.label: Study notes
rows.text: The heat leaving the body also equals −mc dθ, if the body cools without changing state. Dividing by dt gives −mc dθ/dt = K (θ − θ0).  ·  Therefore the rate of fall of temperature is dθ/dt = −(K/mc) (θ − θ0). The constant k = K/(mc) is larger when the body has a small heat capacity.  ·  The minus sign means the temperature falls when θ is above θ0. If the body is cooler than the room, the same equation makes the temperature rise.

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: Role of mc  ·  The surrounding temperature θ0 is constant.  ·  Newton's Law of Cooling — Derivation of Rate of Fall of Temperature is based on fundamental principles.

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: Keep the minus sign until you interpret the rate.  ·  State that the excess is small before quoting the law.  ·  Same surface and same excess: the smaller mc cools faster.

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: The law is a linear approximation. It is used for excesses of a few tens of degrees, where convection and a linearised radiation loss dominate.
